name: Meiosis
kicker: Cell division that halves the chromosome number · Creates sperm and eggs
dates: Happens during the formation of every sperm and egg cell
briefing: Meiosis is the special kind of cell division that creates sperm and egg cells, the body’s sex cells. Unlike ordinary cell division, meiosis divides twice in a row and shuffles genetic material between matching chromosome pairs through crossing over, so the four cells it produces each end up with only half the usual number of chromosomes and a unique genetic mix. That reduction is essential, since fertilization later fuses two of these cells back into a full set.
answerHtml: Meiosis (accept meiosis I or meiosis II; prompt on cell division, oogenesis, or spermatogenesis; do not accept “mitosis”)

tossups.p: Polydactyly caused by Patau syndrome can result from an error during this process, and a Robertsonian translocation, in which two whole chromosomes fuse together, can likewise occur as a mistake during it. A failure of chromosomes to separate properly during it is called nondisjunction.
tossups.r: This process shuffles genetic material through crossing over at X-shaped points called chiasmata. For 10 points, name this form of cell division that produces four haploid daughter cells.

tossups.p: In some species, parthenogenesis lets an egg develop without ever needing a sperm cell from this process to fertilize it. In frogs, a protein called cytostatic factor halts this process partway through, holding an egg cell in place until fertilization finally arrives.
tossups.r: Homologous chromosomes pair up and swap segments of DNA during this process, boosting genetic diversity. For 10 points, name this type of division that creates sperm and egg cells.

tossups.p: German biologist Oskar Hertwig first described this process in 1876 while studying the eggs of sea urchins. In male mammals, it takes place inside the seminiferous tubules of the testes.
tossups.r: It unfolds in two separate rounds of division, with a short pause called interkinesis in between. For 10 points, name this process that halves a cell’s chromosome number to make gametes.

tossups.p: A guardian protein called shugoshin protects a ring-shaped protein called cohesin from being cut apart too early during this process’s first division. The coefficient of coincidence is used to measure how interference reduces the rate of crossing over during it.
tossups.r: Homologous chromosome pairs line up and exchange material at chiasmata. For 10 points, name this cell division that produces four genetically unique cells with half the usual chromosome number.

tossups.p: Four-stranded DNA structures called Holliday junctions form temporarily as chromosomes exchange material during this process. Its long first stage unfolds through leptotene, zygotene, pachytene, diplotene, and diakinesis sub-stages before the chromosomes finally separate.
tossups.r: Nondisjunction, an error during this process, can lead to conditions such as Down syndrome. For 10 points, name this process that produces sperm and egg cells.

tossups.p: Nondisjunction, an error during this process, can cause Turner syndrome, Klinefelter syndrome, or Down syndrome depending on which chromosome pair fails to separate properly. A zipper-like structure called the synaptonemal complex holds paired homologous chromosomes together beforehand.
tossups.r: It produces four genetically unique daughter cells, each with half the usual number of chromosomes. For 10 points, name this type of cell division that creates gametes.

tossups.p: During this process’s zygotene stage, a zipper-like synaptonemal complex assembles to hold homologous chromosomes together. In human females, it produces one usable egg cell plus two or three tiny, nonfunctional polar bodies.
tossups.r: Chromosomes swap segments of DNA in a process called crossing over, increasing genetic diversity. For 10 points, name this cell division that produces sperm and egg cells.

tossups.p: In human egg cells, this process can leave behind up to three tiny, nonfunctional polar bodies alongside the one cell that becomes a usable egg. This process never occurs in bacteria, which lack a nucleus and reproduce asexually instead.
tossups.r: It takes place in two separate rounds of division, with a short pause called interkinesis in between. For 10 points, name this process that halves the chromosome number to form gametes.

tossups.p: During this process’s diplotene stage, the synaptonemal complex breaks back apart, while during its diakinesis stage the paired chromosomes, or tetrads, become clearly visible under a microscope. The haploid cells it produces must later fuse with another haploid cell at fertilization to restore a full set of chromosomes.
tossups.r: Homologous chromosomes exchange material at chiasmata during crossing over. For 10 points, name this cell division that produces four cells with half the usual chromosome number.

tossups.p: This type of division never occurs in bacteria, which reproduce asexually instead, and an error in it called nondisjunction can cause extra fingers or toes through Patau syndrome. A Robertsonian translocation, where two whole chromosomes become fused, is another possible mistake during it.
tossups.r: It involves two separate rounds of division, with a short pause called interkinesis in between. For 10 points, name this process that creates sperm and egg cells.

tossups.p: In frogs, a protein called cytostatic factor arrests this process partway through until fertilization occurs, and a Robertsonian translocation, in which two whole chromosomes fuse together, can occur as an error during it. Parthenogenesis offers some species a way to reproduce without ever completing the usual fertilization step afterward.
tossups.r: This process produces four daughter cells, each haploid, with only half the usual chromosome number. For 10 points, name this cell division that creates gametes.

tossups.p: This process takes place inside the seminiferous tubules of the testes in male mammals, and it was first described in 1876 by German biologist Oskar Hertwig, who studied the eggs of sea urchins. A zipper-like synaptonemal complex holds homologous chromosomes together during an early stage of it.
tossups.r: Crossing over at chiasmata shuffles genetic material between homologous chromosomes. For 10 points, name this process that halves the chromosome number to produce gametes.

tossups.p: The coefficient of coincidence measures how much interference reduces crossing over during this process, while a guardian protein called shugoshin protects cohesin from being cut apart too early during its first division. Four-stranded Holliday junctions briefly form as chromosomes trade material during it.
tossups.r: Nondisjunction, an error in this process, can cause Down, Turner, or Klinefelter syndrome. For 10 points, name this cell division that produces sperm and egg cells.

tossups.p: Four-stranded Holliday junctions briefly form as homologous chromosomes trade material during this process, and nondisjunction, an error during it, can cause Down syndrome or Turner syndrome. Its long first stage passes through leptotene, zygotene, pachytene, diplotene, and diakinesis sub-stages.
tossups.r: It produces four genetically unique daughter cells with half the usual chromosome number. For 10 points, name this process that creates sperm and egg cells.

tossups.p: The haploid cells produced by this process must fuse with another haploid cell at fertilization to rebuild a full set of chromosomes, and a zipper-like synaptonemal complex holds homologous chromosomes together during an early stage of it. This process never occurs in bacteria, which reproduce asexually instead.

trap.title: This process, or mitosis?
trap.body: Mitosis is the other major type of cell division, and the two are constantly mixed up: mitosis makes two identical daughter cells for growth and repair, while this process makes four genetically varied cells with half the chromosome number, for sexual reproduction. Several real tossups explicitly say not to accept or prompt on “mitosis.” Naming the chromosomes themselves, rather than the division process that sorts them, is also marked wrong.
trap.fix: If the clues mention two identical daughter cells, growth, repair, or ordinary body cells, that is mitosis. If the clues mention gametes, haploid cells, crossing over, chiasmata, or a reduction in chromosome number, that is this process.
trap.line: Real answer line: Meiosis [do not accept or prompt on “mitosis”; accept Meiosis I or Meiosis II].
